title: Duplicate Handling Decision Tree
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Data Science
description: Examine seven small tables that contain duplicates, follow a decision tree to the right strategy, and see what each pandas strategy does to the same rows.

educational.topic: Choosing a strategy for duplicate records
learningObjectives: Students will be able to analyze a table that contains duplicate records and select the handling strategy that fits it, justifying the choice with the decision tree.

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Case analysis with a decision tree, with every strategy runnable on the same data for comparison
keyQuestions: In the sales log, the two rows are exactly identical. Why is it still wrong to drop one?
Why do subset=keys and keep='first' produce the same table?
What information does keep='last' throw away in the case of the two partial records?
commonMisconceptions: Duplicate rows are always errors (repeated rows can be real, such as two purchases of the same item).
drop_duplicates() removes rows that share an id (with no subset it removes only rows that match in every column).
Keeping the first or last copy is harmless (it silently discards whatever the other copy said).
assessmentOpportunities: Given a new table with duplicates and a one-line description of where it came from, students name the strategy they would use, write the pandas call, and justify each answer they gave on the way down the tree.
